source.description: Revision plus checked dynamic and native-value JSON implementation, tooling and verification.
source.fingerprint_algorithm: SHA256 over UTF-8 repository-relative paths sorted by encoded byte order, NUL, then binary SHA256 of file bytes. Includes .gn/DEPS/BUILD.gn, .cc/.h/.gn/.gni/.py/.vela under base/benchmarks/build/compiler/runtime/tools/vm, third_party top-level GN files and Unicode manifest/license. Generated files, docs, raw dependency inputs and result JSON are excluded.

comparison_to_previous.basis: Same machine, pinned toolchain, Release flags, VM driver/workloads and measurement settings. Only the five common VM cases are compared.

measurement_limits: Primary VM suites use one-second calibrated samples, nine repetitions and random interleaving; supplemental JSON/dynamic samples use 0.5 seconds and nine repetitions.
Ratios are observations from one Windows x64 machine, not causal speedup claims; inspect the coefficient of variation alongside each median.
JSON decode includes yyjson parsing and native-value construction; encode reuses rooted input, includes traversal and output allocation, and validates the complete output.
first_call_gc_bytes and first_call_objects are accounted GC heap snapshots after one warm operation, not cumulative native allocator traffic or peak resident memory.
JSON throughput is measured in input/output UTF-8 bytes. Payloads contain ordered objects, Unicode strings, mixed arrays and numeric values.
toJson and dynamic workloads include ordinary VM dispatch and GC; dynamic/member_calls and dynamic/typed_boundaries perform 1000 operations per invocation.
All temporary retained_bytes counters are zero after collection; JSON encoding input_heap_bytes remains rooted during measurement.
New JSON/dynamic cases have no pre-feature counterpart. Primitive arrays remain compact; measured ordinary typed-code regressions are retained without normalization.

source.description: Revision plus expanded C++/Vela comparison workloads, correctness/retention checks and baseline documentation in the generated report.
source.fingerprint_algorithm: SHA256 over UTF-8 repository-relative paths sorted by encoded byte order, NUL, then binary SHA256 of file bytes. Includes .gn/DEPS/BUILD.gn, .cc/.h/.gn/.gni/.py/.vela under base/benchmarks/build/compiler/runtime/tools/vm, third_party top-level GN files and Unicode manifest/license. Generated files, docs, raw dependency inputs and result JSON are excluded.

settings.variation: sample standard deviation and coefficient of variation (fraction)

paired_comparison.metric: median VM wall time / median optimized C++ wall time

native_baselines.dynamic_values: Mixed arrays: C++ std::variant<int64_t, string, bool>; Vela dynamic[] with is checks and typed reads.
native_baselines.dynamic_dispatch: Bound calls: C++ std::function with a statically typed signature; Vela resolves a public method on a dynamic receiver and checks the int result. C++ has no runtime member-name lookup.
native_baselines.json_roundtrip: Construct, encode, decode and validate ordered records containing Unicode and mixed arrays. C++ uses pinned yyjson DOM arenas; Vela uses native Map/dynamic[] graphs, runtime checks and GC. The ratio includes these representation and contract differences, not only bytecode execution.
native_baselines.byte_data_little: Zeroed byte buffer, unaligned 64-bit stores/loads and an owner-alias check; C++ vector<byte>/memcpy with explicit little endian.
native_baselines.byte_data_big: Zeroed byte buffer, unaligned 64-bit stores/loads and an owner-alias check; C++ vector<byte>/memcpy with explicit big endian.
native_baselines.regexp_records: Both compile pinned PCRE2 with UTF/UCP, matching newline/BSR settings, interpreter budgets and no JIT. Build Unicode input, collect nonempty matches, convert coordinates to code points, copy captures and parse numbers inside timing.
native_baselines.numeric_parse: Format integers, parse decimal int/double values, verify the fraction and accumulate. C++ uses from_chars and pinned Abseil SimpleAtod; inputs are valid decimal strings.
native_baselines.ascii_case: Construct ASCII strings and verify upper/lower round trips. C++ uses ASCII character mapping; this workload makes no Unicode-casing comparison.
native_baselines.utc_roundtrip: Construct UTC timestamps, format canonical milliseconds, parse and inspect calendar fields. C++ uses pinned Abseil Time; inputs are valid canonical UTC strings, not the complete Vela error/range contract.

comparison_to_previous.basis: The previous entry measures five CPU-time VM microbenchmarks and standalone JSON/dynamic APIs; this entry measures complete C++/VM paired workloads using wall time. No cross-suite regression ratio is computed.

measurement_limits: Eighteen workloads at two input sizes: 36 C++/VM pairs and 36 separate Vela compilation cases; every case has seven randomly interleaved repetitions.
Execution excludes Vela compilation and shared integer-input preparation; workload-local containers, strings, library compilation, checksums, cleanup and ordinary GC are included.
C++ kernels use the same logical inputs and expected results, compile in separate translation units with Release /O2, and may inline or vectorize native work.
JSON, dynamic and API ratios include the documented native representation and validation differences; they are not isolated measurements of VM instruction dispatch.
The ASCII casing case does not compare full Unicode casing. Date input is canonical UTC, not the full invalid-input or range-checking contract.
VM baseline and retained counters include rooted input and constants. Every VM sample returns to its baseline after collection; snapshots are not peak memory, RSS or C++ allocator accounting.
Single Windows x64 machine. Scheduling, frequency and allocation noise affect ratios; use the retained per-case variation and do not infer a language-wide average.
Prior standalone parse/encode/dynamic measurements remain in the previous entry; they are not presented as measurements of the new paired suite.
